title: Finite type module sheaves have finite local coefficient expansions
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space and $\mathcal F$ a finite type sheaf of modules [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. For each $x\in X$ there are an open neighbourhood $U$, an integer $n\geq0$, and sections $s_j\in\mathcal F(U)$ indexed by $\mathrm{Fin}(n)$ such that for every open $W\subseteq U$, section $t\in\mathcal F(W)$, and point $y\in W$, there is an open neighbourhood $V$ of $y$ contained in $W$ and coefficients $a_j\in\mathcal O_X(V)$ with $t|_V=\sum_j a_j(s_j|_V)$.

source.place: Modules, Definition 01B5, proof of Lemma 01B8, and local lifting in Section 01AF, Lemma 01AG

proof.text: Choose finite local generators data from finite type and a member U of its covering containing x. Evaluate its generating sections at the terminal object of Over U and reindex the finite family by Fin n.

The generating map from the free sheaf to F.over U is epi. Forget to abelian sheaves, which preserves epimorphisms, and apply the local-surjectivity criterion. The covering sieve on Over U corresponds to a covering sieve of opens; choose a member V containing y and a preimage z of the restriction of t. The Lean proof uses Mathlib Sheaf.isLocallySurjective_iff_epi' and Sieve.overEquiv directly, not the project local-lifting lemma.

The free sheaf on a finite family is a biproduct of unit sheaves. Its total identity writes z as the sum of inclusions of its coordinates. Linearity of the generating map identifies its image with the stated sum of coordinate multiples of restricted generators. This includes the zero-generator and empty-open cases.

lean.statement: theorem exists_finite_type_local_coefficients (X : RingedSpace.{u}) (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X)) (x : X) [F.IsFiniteType] : ∃ (U : Opens X), x ∈ U ∧ ∃ (n : ℕ) (s : Fin n → F.val.obj (op U)), ∀ (W : Opens X) (hW : W ≤ U) (t : F.val.obj (op W)) (y : X), y ∈ W → ∃ (V : Opens X) (hV : V ≤ W), y ∈ V ∧ ∃ a : Fin n → (moduleRings X).obj.obj (op V), F.val.map (homOfLE hV).op t = ∑ j, a j • F.val.map (homOfLE (hV.trans hW)).op (s j)
